material_systems.name: Solvent-Based MDF Edge Sealer

primer.notes: MUST be applied to MDF cut/routed edges BEFORE any latex product. Water-based primers cause irreversible fiber swelling on MDF edges. Step 1 of two-step MDF prime. Architectural element MDF edges: beam miters, column panel joints, mantel shelf edges, leg edges.

material_systems.notes: Edge-only application. Step 1 of MDF two-step prime process. NON-NEGOTIABLE sequence.

material_systems.name: High-Build Latex Face Primer for MDF

primer.notes: Applied to MDF face surfaces AFTER edge sealing with shellac/oil-based. Builds film, levels surface. Step 2 of two-step MDF prime.

material_systems.notes: Step 2 of MDF two-step prime. Face surfaces only — edges already sealed.

material_systems.name: Stain-Blocking Primer for FJP/Poplar

products: Benjamin Moore Fresh Start Oil-Based Primer
primer.notes: MANDATORY for bare FJP. Resin and green mineral streaks bleed through standard latex primers without stain-blocking. NOT optional. Per Millwork_NC_Paint_Doctrine SS4.1.

material_systems.notes: Substrate-driven. Stain-blocking is not optional for FJP architectural elements.

material_systems.name: Tannin-Blocking Primer for Hardwood

primer.notes: Blocks tannin bleed-through on bare hardwood (oak, cherry, walnut). Per Millwork Doctrine SS4. Common on premium mantel assemblies and solid-wood columns.

material_systems.notes: Substrate-driven. Required for all bare hardwood architectural element substrates.

primer.notes: Standard primer-sealer for bare softwood elements.

material_systems.name: Standard Acrylic Trim Enamel

products: Sherwin-Williams ProClassic Waterborne Interior Acrylic Enamel
Benjamin Moore Regal Select Interior Semi-Gloss
finish.notes: Fast dry/recoat. Non-yellowing. Water cleanup. Same system as all other fine finish millwork specs.

material_systems.notes: QT3 — satin is the only sheen per sheen/QT gate (FFD SS4.1). Material systems are recommendations — contractor has discretion (RC-005).

material_systems.name: Modified Urethane Trim Enamel

products: Benjamin Moore Advance Waterborne Interior Alkyd
Sherwin-Williams Pro Industrial Waterbased Alkyd Urethane
finish.notes: Superior flow and leveling. SHORT working time — apply, tip once, walk away (FFD SS15.3.1). Vertical column faces and beam undersides are prone to sags with this product — apply in thin coats.

material_systems.notes: QT4. Material systems are recommendations — contractor has discretion (RC-005).

material_systems.name: Premium Urethane Trim Enamel

finish.coat_notes: QT5 brush typically requires 3+ coats per FFD SS15.10.3.
finish.notes: Maximum durability. Excellent leveling. Emerald Urethane is acrylic-urethane enamel, NOT waterborne alkyd (RC-006).

material_systems.notes: QT5. Gloss available only at this tier. Material systems are recommendations — contractor has discretion (RC-005).

coverage_profiles.notes: Architectural element primer coverage. For beams: effective SF depends on beam profile (3-sided box). For columns: effective SF depends on column perimeter x height. For mantels: effective SF depends on assembly complexity. All coverage based on effective SF of the element, not raw input units.
assumptions: Single coat primer system (except MDF two-step: edge seal + face prime)
Coverage expressed per effective SF of element surfaces

coverage_profiles.notes: Finish coat coverage on primed smooth millwork surfaces. Two-coat standard; third coat at QT5 brush. Profile complexity (ornate beams, fluted columns, full assembly mantels) increases effective surface area and material consumption.
assumptions: Beam LF converted to effective SF via profile width factor at estimation time
Column EA converted to effective SF via column perimeter x height at estimation time
Mantel EA converted to effective SF via assembly surface area at estimation time

consumables.name: Canvas drop cloth
consumables.usage: Localized floor protection in spray work zone or perimeter runners for brush
consumables.notes: Spray: localized floor coverage around each element (floor_workzone — not full room). Brush: perimeter runners along work path for drip protection (floor_perimeter). Less material than room-spanning specs because elements are discrete.

consumables.name: Masking tape (1.5" blue painter's tape)
consumables.usage: Wall adjacent masking near spray target, fixture masking, general edge masking
consumables.notes: 60 yards = 180 LF per roll. Wall masking at beam-wall, column-wall, mantel-wall junctions (spray only). Fixture masking near beam spray work.

consumables.name: Masking paper (12-inch)
consumables.usage: Wall surface masking near element-wall junction (spray only)
consumables.notes: Paper + tape system for wall surface protection near element spray zones. 12-inch width covers wall area adjacent to beam/column/mantel junction.

consumables.name: Plastic sheeting (lightweight)
consumables.usage: Fixture bagging near beam spray work
consumables.notes: Lightweight plastic for fixture bagging near spray target. Ceiling fixtures near beam work zone.

consumables.name: Sandpaper 150-grit
consumables.usage: Pre-primer sanding for bare substrates, factory primer scuff
consumables.notes: 150 grit for initial bare substrate sanding and factory primer scuff. Beam overhead faces require pole sander or ladder work.

consumables.name: Sandpaper 220-grit
consumables.usage: Pre-primer final sand, between-coat sanding (QT3 spot, QT4 full)
consumables.notes: 220 grit for final prep sand and between-coat sanding. Rigid sanding block mandatory (FFD SS15.4.1). Profile detail on ornate beams, fluted columns, and mantel molding requires flexible sanding sponge.

consumables.name: Sandpaper 320-grit
consumables.notes: 220-320 grit range at QT5. Uniform scratch pattern required.

consumables.name: Sanding block (fine grit range)
consumables.usage: Rigid block for between-coat sanding. Mandatory per FFD SS15.4.1.
consumables.notes: One block per crew, reusable. Critical for flat faces of beams, columns, and mantel surfaces.

consumables.name: Angled sash brush (2-2.5")
consumables.usage: Primary brush for element detail and cutting-in at junctions
consumables.notes: 2-2.5 inch for beam profile detail, column detail, mantel shelf and leg detail. One per painter per material change. Also used for cut-in at element-wall junctions during spray method.

consumables.name: Angled sash brush (1.5")
consumables.usage: Detail brush for tight profiles — fluted columns, ornate beam detail, mantel molding
consumables.notes: Smaller brush for tight detail areas. Used on ornate/fluted profiles regardless of primary application method.

consumables.name: Mini roller (4-inch, microfiber or foam)
consumables.usage: Roll and Tip method for flat column faces and mantel shelf surfaces (brush method)
consumables.notes: Per FFD SS15.6 Roll and Tip method. Apply with mini roller, then tip with brush for leveling. Works well on flat column faces and mantel shelf surfaces.

consumables.name: Airless spray tip 310-411
consumables.usage: Fine atomization for architectural element spray finish
consumables.notes: Tight fan pattern for millwork detail. Multiple passes at different angles for beam undersides and column profiles.

consumables.name: Tack cloth
consumables.usage: Remove sanding dust before each coat application
consumables.notes: One tack cloth covers ~30 SF of element surface. Use before every coat. Work into profile detail.

consumables.name: Paintable acrylic latex caulk
consumables.usage: Element-to-structure junctions (beam-ceiling, column-floor/ceiling, mantel-wall) and internal joints
consumables.notes: Significant caulk consumption on architectural elements. Beams: beam-to-ceiling full length + beam-to-wall at ends + miter joints. Columns: column-to-ceiling perimeter + column-to-floor perimeter + column-to-wall (wall-mounted). Mantels: mantel-to-wall all contact edges + shelf-to-leg joints. Use flexible painter's caulk for movement-prone junctions.

consumables.name: Lightweight spackle compound
consumables.usage: Fill fastener holes on architectural elements
consumables.notes: Fill nail holes, screw holes, minor surface defects. Beam and column fastener density varies by construction method. Overfill-sand-flush method.

consumables.name: Sandable wood filler
consumables.usage: Fill deeper defects, damaged edges, and knot holes
consumables.notes: Supplement to spackle for deeper fills. May be needed at beam miter joints, column panel joints, and mantel leg-to-shelf joints.

consumables.name: Safe-release masking tape
consumables.usage: Masking near finished surfaces (stone/brick fireplace surround near mantel)
consumables.notes: Low-tack tape for masking at mantel-to-fireplace-surround junction. Protects stone/brick/tile from paint contact without damaging surface finish.

floor_perimeter.description: Perimeter drop cloth runners near element work area for brush drip protection

floor_workzone.description: Localized floor coverage around element spray target
floor_workzone.notes: Discrete element protection — not full room. Cover floor directly below and around each element.

wall_adjacent.description: Wall masking near element-wall junctions (beam-wall, column-wall, mantel-wall)

fixture_covers.description: Ceiling fixture masking near beam spray work
fixture_covers.condition: application_method = spray AND fixtures near beam work area

required_inputs.purpose: Beam running LF for material estimation
Fixture count for masking near beam spray
Wall masking LF near element-wall junctions (spray)

compatibility_rules.description: All finish systems are compatible with all primer systems
compatibility_rules.notes: Primer and finish are independent selections. All combinations valid.

compatibility_rules.description: SS_PRIMED_FACTORY compatible with all finish systems
compatibility_rules.notes: Scuff sand factory primer for adhesion. No additional primer needed.

compatibility_rules.description: MDF two-step prime: shellac edge seal MUST precede latex face prime
compatibility_rules.notes: SYS_PRIMER_MDF_SHELLAC on edges first, then SYS_PRIMER_MDF_LATEX on faces. Never reverse. Applies to MDF beam shells, column panels, mantel components.

risk_notes.topic: MDF fiber swelling on element edges
risk_notes.risk: Irreversible fiber swelling if water-based product contacts raw MDF cut/routed edges
risk_notes.mitigation: Always seal MDF edges with shellac/oil-based sealer (SYS_PRIMER_MDF_SHELLAC) before any latex product. Architectural elements have many exposed edges: beam miters, column panel joints, mantel shelf edges.

risk_notes.risk: Resin and green mineral streaks bleed through non-stain-blocking primer on bare FJP
risk_notes.mitigation: Use SYS_PRIMER_POPLAR_STAINBLOCK. Stain-blocking is MANDATORY for bare FJP.

risk_notes.risk: Tannin bleed re-emerges through multiple finish coats on bare hardwood mantels or columns
risk_notes.mitigation: Use SYS_PRIMER_HARDWOOD_TANNINBLOCK. Required for all bare hardwood substrates.

risk_notes.topic: Sag/run on vertical column faces and beam undersides
risk_notes.risk: Over-application on vertical or overhead surfaces creates sags, especially with waterborne alkyd products (short open time)
risk_notes.mitigation: Thin coats on vertical column faces and beam undersides. With Advance/urethane products: apply, tip once, walk away (FFD SS15.3.1). Do not overwork.

risk_notes.risk: Spray overspray reaches finished walls, ceiling, stone/brick surround near mantel
risk_notes.mitigation: Full masking at all element-to-adjacent-surface junctions. Paper + tape system. Verify masking seal before spraying. Safe-release tape near stone/brick.

risk_notes.topic: Paint build-up in inside corners and detail profiles
risk_notes.risk: Excessive buildup in beam box corners, fluted column channels, ornate mantel molding recesses
risk_notes.mitigation: Light spray passes on detail areas. Brush out excess in corners while wet. Start with recessed detail, then flat surfaces.

material_notes.dual_system_architecture: TWO independent material system layers: (1) Primer systems are substrate-driven with 5 distinct paths. (2) Finish systems are QT-driven. Identical architecture to SF_WOOD_CEILING_NC, SF_WOOD_WALL_NC, SF_WAINSCOT_PANEL_NC.
material_notes.element_material_estimation: Material quantity estimation for architectural elements requires converting input units (LF for beams, EA for columns/mantels) to effective SF using profile/size factors. This conversion happens at estimation runtime using PaintScope data, not in this material definition.
material_notes.caulk_consumption_note: Architectural elements have higher caulk consumption per item than typical trim due to larger junction perimeters. Beams: full-length ceiling junction. Columns: full-perimeter ceiling + floor junctions. Mantels: full-contact wall junctions.
material_notes.localized_protection_note: Protection for spray is LOCALIZED (floor_workzone) not full room (floor_full). Architectural elements are discrete items. Less protection material than room-spanning specs (ceiling, wall) but more concentrated per element.
material_notes.product_classification: Advance is waterborne alkyd. Emerald Urethane is acrylic-urethane enamel (RC-006).

assumptions.value: 350-450 SF/gal for finish coat on primed smooth surface
assumptions.source: Manufacturer PDS data, aligned with all fine finish spec coverage
Standard manufacturer yield for 10.1 oz caulk tube at 3/16" bead
